options_considered: General healthcare billing vs laboratory billing
rationale: Laboratory billing combines high claim volume with multi-payer adjudication and frequent corrections; matches applicant's professional context
limitations: Scope is domain-focused; generalization outside lab billing not claimed

options_considered: Forced single-best link vs uncertainty-preserving tiers
rationale: Multi-source billing records contain genuinely ambiguous cases; forcing picks injects errors silently
limitations: Review queue volume must be monitored against manual capacity

topic: Participating sites for the study data contract
chosen: Three real CLIA-certified laboratories with distinct ownership models
rationale: Multi-site structure forces cross-org identifier isolation and tests generalization assumptions
limitations: Site tokens denote the participating organizations under the data-use arrangement

options_considered: Final cash collection vs first observable payment/closure event
chosen: First observable positive allocation or no-payment closure within H days
rationale: Final collection depends on unobservable banking events; first observable event is operationally actionable and labelable
evidence_basis: Deep Claim response-date framing (PW06); Fine-Gray competing events (PW04)
limitations: H=30d and landmark=7d are study defaults pending operational confirmation (unknowns U03/U04)

options_considered: Continuous-time survival vs discrete-time interval conditional probabilities
rationale: Irregular observation windows and daily operational cadence fit discrete intervals; three-class sum-to-one constraint is testable (T16)
limitations: Continuous-time extensions not implemented; not claimed
